hints: Look closely at the first diagram and notice the difference between the thick-walled outer cells and the thin-walled inner cells. Which side do you think can stretch or shrink more easily when water moves?

The solution with the highest water potential is the most dilute, so water will move into the cells by osmosis. Think about which side becomes longer when fully turgid and how strongly the strip would curl.
walkthrough:
**Observe the strip structure**

The scape wall has two faces. The outside is made of thick-walled outer cells that resist stretching. The inside is made of thin-walled inner cells that stretch and shrink easily.

Think of it like two rulers glued together, one stretchy and one stiff.

**Apply water potential and osmosis**

Water always moves from higher water potential to lower water potential by osmosis.
$$\text{high } \Psi \text{ solution} \rightarrow \text{low } \Psi \text{ cells}$$
The highest water potential sucrose solution is the most dilute. It causes the greatest net movement of water into both types of cells, making them fully turgid.

**Link turgidity to differential expansion and curling**

When turgid, the thin-walled inner cells expand in length much more than the thick-walled outer cells. The inner face therefore becomes longer and convex, while the outer face stays shorter and concave.

The more water taken up, the greater the length difference and the stronger the curl in that direction. Slight curl means slight uptake, strong curl means maximum uptake.

**Pick the most turgid curl**

Both A and B curl with inner cells convex (longer) and outer cells concave (shorter), so both are turgid. A shows the strongest curl in that direction, so it has taken up the most water.

Therefore A is the piece from the highest water potential solution.

options.A: Correct. Inner cells are convex and longer, outer cells are concave and shorter, with strong curvature. This shows maximum expansion of thin-walled inner cells, so maximum water uptake from the highest water potential.
options.B: False. This also shows inner longer than outer but the strip is almost straight, so only slight turgidity. It would be from a solution with slightly high water potential, not the highest.
options.C: False. This shows outer longer than inner, the opposite curl, meaning slight water loss and slight plasmolysis. It would be from a solution with slightly low water potential.
options.D: False. This shows strong curl with outer convex and longer and inner concave and shorter, meaning maximum shrinkage of inner cells. It would be from the lowest water potential with greatest water loss.
